entries.name: Beveled leader-body diagram

alignment.method: Robust least-squares fit to midpoints between the upper and lower native shank edges, excluding the beveled end and right terminal; one rigid rotation of all contours.

entries.identity_reason: The printed six/eight/ten-point body diagrams illustrate one beveled leader-body construction. Their nominal body widths, drawn curvature and length-to-height differences remain in individual witness records, not separate design IDs. Existing Baltimore space rules have a different thin-stroke and turned-end construction; they are not replacement sources.
entries.quality_todo: Seek a sharper intact matching beveled body illustration during remaining surveys. Preserve printed curvature and small native ink holes; the final family/browser proof remains pending the whole-library gate.

recipe.notes: Complete six-point leader-body illustration, identified by the printed BODY column. One canonical construction retains separate six/eight/ten-point witnesses and their curvature and aspect variations. The six-point impression has less ink loss. Native uniform scaling and one measured rigid shank rotation; tiny disconnected paper components below64nativepixels removed; source holes retained, no analytic silhouette substituted.

measurement.method: Largest native component at threshold215, median upper/lower shank edges over x84–319, horizontal left boundary relative to the leftmost tip. Uniform height normalization is for comparison only; native geometry is preserved in drawing recipes.

classification: The printed FACE and BODY headings separate a printing surface from the illustration of its metal body. This item preserves the technical body illustration. Nominal body size and small drawing variations do not create additional design identities.
quality_choice: The six-point impression has less internal ink loss than the eight-point terminal and ten-point upper edge; all three complete native witnesses remain available.
